Song removal and recorded use: ranks

A descriptive analysis of The Sacred Harp, 1991 Denson Edition

October 19, 2026

Results

A logistic classification model relates song-use annual ranks to the removal decisions for the 2025 edition. The repertoire contains 557 songs: 79 removed and 478 kept. The model is fitted to the complete repertoire, and all results below describe that full-data fit.

At a removal-probability threshold of 0.2824, the model identifies 56 of the 79 removed songs (70.9%) and correctly classifies 447 of the 478 kept songs. It classifies 31 kept songs as removed and 23 removed songs as kept. Overall, 54 classifications differ from the recorded decisions.

Persistent low ranking has the largest standardized coefficient. A one-standard-deviation increase in the fraction of historical years spent in the bottom 79 multiplies fitted removal odds by 1.57, conditional on the other predictors. Worse recent and historical mean ranks are also associated with greater removal probability.

Long-term rank trend (+0.076) and recent change in rank (-0.026) carry smaller coefficients than the popularity and bottom-79 measures. Recent and historical ranks are correlated (0.94), so coefficients should be interpreted jointly.

The threshold maximizes F1 across the 557 fitted outcomes, with the higher threshold breaking an exact tie. The reported precision, recall, F1 and classification counts use that threshold. The probability-ranking measures use the continuous fitted scores.

Actual decisionClassified as keptClassified as removedTotal
Kept44731478

Classifying every song as kept would give 85.8% accuracy and identify none of the removals. A constant score has average precision 0.142. Among the 79 highest fitted removal probabilities, 51 songs were actually removed (64.6%). This fixed-size ranking calculation is separate from the F1 threshold; song keys break probability ties.

Contribution of the other four predictors

To measure what rank levels and trends contribute beyond persistent low popularity, compare the five-predictor model with logistic regression using only historical bottom-79 frequency. Both models are fitted to all 557 songs, standardize their inputs, and use the same L2 regularization parameter, C = 0.01. Each model’s classification threshold maximizes its own full-data F1.

Adding recent mean rank, historical mean rank, long-term rank trend and recent rank change raises average precision from 0.611 to 0.651: an increase of 0.040, or 6.5% relative to the one-feature model. ROC AUC rises from 0.891 to 0.921. Brier score falls from 0.089 to 0.080, a 10.3% reduction in mean squared probability error.

MeasureBottom-79 frequency onlyAll five predictorsChange

ROC AUC0.8910.921+0.029
Precision56.1%64.4%+8.3 percentage points
Recall75.9%70.9%-5.1 percentage points
F10.6450.675+0.030
Accuracy88.2%90.3%+2.2 percentage points
Brier score (lower is better)0.0890.080-0.009

The improvement in classification is modest. The one-feature model identifies 60 of the 79 removals; the full model identifies 56 at its own F1 threshold. Kept songs flagged as removed number 47 for the one-feature model and 31 for the full model. The net reduction in classification errors is 12. At the song level, 16 classifications become correct and 4 become incorrect.

This comparison measures the four predictors’ combined contribution to the descriptive fit. It does not allocate the gain among the individual predictors. The precision–recall curve and probability-error measures capture improvements beyond the particular classification thresholds.

Comparison statistics, one-feature model parameters and per-song results; comparison figure in SVG format.

Data and predictors

Annual song-use statistics are drawn from singings using the 1991 Denson Edition as their primary book. The analysis uses 1995–2019 for historical measures and 2022–2024 for recent measures. Years 2020–2021 are omitted because of pandemic disruption. The 2025 figures and Overall columns are excluded because they include use after removal decisions could have been made or announced.

PredictorDefinition
Recent mean rankAverage annual rank, 2022–2024.
Historical mean rankAverage annual rank, 1995–2019.
Long-term rank trendOLS slope of annual rank against year, 1995–2019, in rank positions per year.
Recent change in rankMean rank in 2022–2024 minus mean rank in 2015–2019.
Historical bottom-79 frequencyFraction of years 1995–2019 at rank 479 or worse.

Larger rank numbers indicate lower popularity. Positive rank trends and recent changes indicate worsening relative standing. Source ranks are competition ranks: tied songs share the best position in their tied group.

The bottom-79 cutoff follows the 79 removals in this repertoire. It denotes the lowest 79 rank positions among 557 songs (14.18%), or rank 479 and worse. If a tied group crosses the boundary, fewer than 79 songs can qualify in that year. This feature does not constrain the model to classify exactly 79 songs as removed.

Model specification

The outcome is removal from the 2025 edition: removed = 1 and kept = 0. The model is logistic regression with an intercept and an L2 penalty, using regularization parameter C = 0.01. Each of the five predictors is standardized using its mean and standard deviation across the 557 songs. No class weighting is applied. Fitted probabilities are obtained by applying the logistic function to the intercept plus the weighted standardized predictors.

PredictorStandardized coefficientOdds ratio per standard deviation
Recent mean rank+0.3351.397
Historical mean rank+0.3211.378
Long-term rank trend+0.0761.079
Recent change in rank-0.0260.974
Historical bottom-79 frequency+0.4481.565

A positive coefficient corresponds to higher fitted removal odds; a negative coefficient corresponds to lower odds, holding the other predictors fixed. Correlation among predictors limits how separately their coefficients can be interpreted.

Interpretation

The results quantify the association between recorded song use and the observed removal decisions within this repertoire. The committee also considered information about leaders and made musical and individual judgments. Those factors are not measured here, so a song’s fitted probability does not establish why it was kept or removed.

The statistics reflect the singings represented in the minutes. Changes in reporting coverage can affect use measures, and a zero recorded count does not prove a song was never sung. Exact committee decision dates are unavailable. Removal labels follow the publisher’s list with 24t and 25 marked removed as supplied corrections. The publisher also lists 467 (LISBON) as removed, noting replacement by Read’s original fuging arrangement.

Sources and analysis files

FaSoLa: song use in the 1991 Denson Edition; Sacred Harp Publishing Company: songs removed for the 2025 edition.

Model parameters, feature definitions and classification threshold; song-level data; figures in SVG format. Companion analysis using counts.
